name: Tank as One Whole: Pipe Rates and Partial Filling
description: Turn a pipe time into a one-hour rate, then use that rate for whole or partial tanks.
script_scope: Teach the one-tank model: if a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its rate is 1/x tank per hour; if an outlet empties in y hours, its rate is −1/y. Start with one pipe, then partial tanks and remaining fractions, and connect fraction-per-hour language to litres-per-minute language. Include questions where a tank is already partly full, where only part of a tank must be emptied, and where a start clock time is converted into a finish time. The learner should always identify the amount of tank still to be filled or emptied before dividing by the net rate.

name: Multiple Inlets and Outlets: Net Rate
description: Add filling rates, subtract emptying rates, and decide whether the water level rises or falls.
script_scope: Teach combined-pipe questions by adding inlet rates and subtracting outlet rates. Cover two inlets, two inlets plus an outlet, one inlet plus a stronger outlet, three or more pipes, and questions asking how many identical inlet/waste pipes are present. Include a contribution-share question where several inlet pipes carry different liquids and the learner finds the fraction supplied by one pipe. Require a direction check first: positive net rate means filling, negative net rate means emptying.

name: Leaks and Waste Pipes: Find the Hidden Rate
description: Use the difference between normal and actual filling to recover the rate of a leak or waste pipe.
script_scope: Teach leaks as hidden outlets. Compare a pipe's normal fill rate with the slower observed net fill rate to obtain the leak rate. Cover finding leak-emptying time, finding a waste-pipe rate from two filling pipes and a combined time, tank capacity from a known litre-per-minute inlet plus leakage, and a leak that appears only after part of the tank is filled. Include late discovery of an open waste pipe. Keep signs meaningful: a negative contribution means water leaves the tank.

name: Pipe Efficiency, Diameter, and Equivalent Pipes
description: Convert efficiency, diameter, and groups of identical pipes into comparable flow rates.
script_scope: Teach that efficiency is proportional to rate and inversely proportional to time. Cover statements such as one pipe being twice or three times as fast as another, chains such as C twice B and B twice A, and multiple identical pipes. Include the chapter relation that for similar pipes flow is proportional to the square of diameter, so filling/emptying time is inversely proportional to diameter squared. Extend to hot/cold groups and bucket-capacity analogies. Emphasize converting all pipes to one common rate unit before combining them.

name: Reverse Pipe Problems and Unknown Times
description: Recover individual pipe times from together-times, differences, ratios, or pairwise information.
script_scope: Teach reverse-rate algebra. Cover one known pipe plus a together-time, individual times differing by a fixed number of hours, one pipe being a multiple of another, pairwise rates, and questions where the unknown appears in a reciprocal equation that becomes quadratic. Use positive-time checks to reject impossible roots. Include a pump whose fill and empty capacities differ by a fixed rate and whose times differ by a fixed amount. Learners should form rate equations from the story rather than guess times.

name: Staged Filling: Pipes Open or Close Midway
description: Split the tank into time stages when pipes join, close, or a water level triggers a change.
script_scope: Teach piecewise tank problems. Cover two pipes starting together and one closing, an outlet closing before the tank is full, a second inlet opening after half the tank is filled, pipes opening at different clock times, and a pipe or leak activated when the water reaches a stated fraction. Each stage should have its own active-pipe rate and its own amount of tank handled. Emphasize that the next stage begins with the water already accumulated or lost in earlier stages.

name: Alternating and Successive Pipe Schedules
description: Use cycle work for pipes opened alternately or successively in a repeating order.
script_scope: Teach repeating schedules by finding the work done in one full cycle, counting complete cycles, then handling the leftover fraction in the correct turn order. Cover two alternating inlets, an inlet alternating with an outlet, A always open while B and C alternate, three pipes opened successively for equal intervals, and staggered openings with fixed time gaps. Include clock-time answers and cases where the final partial cycle ends before every pipe gets another turn.

name: Tank Capacity, Flow, Storage, and Special Applications
description: Connect pipe rates to litres, tank dimensions, steady supply, storage limits, and mixed liquids.
script_scope: Apply pipe-rate reasoning to physical flow and storage. Cover litres per minute, finding tank capacity from a fractional rate, rectangular tank volume, water rise from a pipe of known cross-section and speed, bucket capacity, steady supply versus varying demand, sustainable daily use with constant replenishment, and the fraction of one liquid in a tank filled by several inlet pipes. Include unit conversion where required, but keep the pipe-rate idea visible rather than turning the lesson into geometry alone.

name: Data Sufficiency for Pipes and Cisterns
description: Decide whether statements give enough independent rate information to answer a pipe question.
script_scope: Teach data sufficiency using the chapter's two-statement and three-statement patterns. Cover when both fill and empty times are needed, when either of two different descriptions independently determines a rate, when a tank capacity is irrelevant because only fractional rates matter, and when one of several statements is redundant. Include questions involving efficiency ratios, together-time, leakage, and litre-per-minute taps. The goal is to judge sufficiency without doing unnecessary calculation.
